summary: A calibration evaluated on its own fit sample could pass: calibration.py recorded no sample check and the validator compared fit and evaluation sample names only as exact strings.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the first release of calibration.py and of the ml-artifact calibration block and its exact-name rule

observables: the calibration block of an ml-artifact and its ml.calibration_on_fit_sample verdict
reported calibration metrics (ECE, reliability) of a calibrated classifier
impact.bias: calibration metrics computed on the sample the map was fit on are optimistic (the source brief's same-sample isotonic map gave ECE 6.5e-17), and validation did not catch it when the two names differed in whitespace, './' or case, or when one file was a copy of the other
impact.trigger: calibration.py run with --eval on the --fit sample (or a copy of it), with no event-id check, and the two sample names not exactly equal

remedy: rerun calibration.py with a release that has the fix (with --id-col) on disjoint fit and evaluation samples, and validate the artifact again
